text: The chest X-ray showing bilateral interstitial infiltrates is a significant finding. Given your lack of fever and normal white blood cell count, this points toward a chronic process rather than an acute infection. Have you noticed a progressive decline in your lung function over the past few years, or do you have a history of exposure to dust, chemicals, or bird droppings?

speaker: Patient
text: I don't recall a gradual decline over the years, but I have worked as a mechanic for many years, so I've been around a lot of dust and chemicals. I haven't had any specific exposure to bird droppings that I can think of.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for mentioning your work as a mechanic; exposure to silica dust or metal fumes is a strong risk factor. To further characterize the nature of your cough and rule out other causes, do you produce any sputum, and if so, what color is it? REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary_Function_Tests (PFTs)

text: RESULTS: Pulmonary_Function_Tests: Reduced FVC and FEV1 with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, indicating a restrictive pattern.

speaker: Doctor
text: The PFT results confirming a restrictive pattern, combined with your history of mechanic work and the X-ray findings, strongly suggest an occupational lung disease. Given your specific exposure to dust and chemicals, do you have any history of skin rashes, joint pain, or muscle weakness that might indicate a connective tissue involvement?

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Occupational Pulmonary Fibrosis (likely due to silica or metal fume exposure).
